code: get_sumstats <- function(G, pheno, interaction = FALSE, E = NULL) {   betas <- numeric(ncol(G))   ses <- numeric(ncol(G))    for (i in seq_len(ncol(G))) {     if (interaction) {       model <- lm(pheno ~ G[, i] + E + G[, i]:E)       betas[i] <- coef(model)[4]       ses[i] <- summary(model)$coefficients[4, 2]     } else {       model <- lm(pheno ~ G[, i])       betas[i] <- coef(model)[2]       ses[i] <- summary(model)$coefficients[2, 2]     }   }    list(beta = betas, se = ses) }

title: Part 1: Introduction
text: Welcome MERLIN (MEndelian Randomization Linear INteraction) package. Traditional Mendelian Randomization (MR) relies genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics infer average causal effect exposure outcome. However, increasingly recognized causal effects may uniform across populations rather exhibit heterogeneity driven environmental factors. MERLIN designed estimate causal effect heterogeneity. systematically integrating summary statistics GWAS Genome-Wide Interaction Studies (GWIS), MERLIN provides robust statistical framework evaluate environmental variables modulate causal pathway exposure outcome. Key Features Summary-Data Driven: requires GWAS GWIS summary statistics, bypassing need individual-level genotype data (often restricted due privacy concerns). Robust Framework: Effectively accounts sample overlap linkage disequilibrium (LD) among instrumental variables. Comprehensive Output: Provides estimates, standard errors, p-values main causal effect interaction (heterogeneity) effect.

title: Part 4: Data Preprocessing and Instrumental Variable Selection
text: ivselect function core preprocessing component. selects instrumental variables using Linkage Disequilibrium (LD) clumping extracts effect sizes standard errors downstream analysis. Detailed Parameter Interpretations customize clumping regularizing process, ivselect utilizes following parameters: plink_dir: Local path PLINK executable. set NULL, package automatically downloads appropriate version OS. pval_cutoff_gwas / pval_cutoff_gwis: Significance thresholds extracting potential IVs GWAS GWIS respectively. r2_cutoff: r^2 threshold LD clumping. SNPs correlations higher value within specified physical distance clumped. kb_cutoff: physical distance window (kilobases) used LD clumping. maf_cutoff: Minor Allele Frequency threshold quality control. lam: Shrinkage turning parameter (\lambda) used regularizing estimated LD correlation matrix guarantee positive definiteness. coreNum: Number CPU cores allocated parallel processing speed calculation genomic blocks. intersect_mode: Logical flag. TRUE, instruments must pass thresholds GWAS GWIS (intersection). FALSE, instruments passing thresholds either GWAS GWIS included (union, default). Running ivselect console output shows progress IV selection. title: Part 5: Model Fitting and Convergence Diagnostics
text: MERLIN employs Bayesian framework (Gibbs sampling) estimate posterior distributions causal effects. primary MERLIN function highly flexible, offering various model specifications accommodate different biological assumptions environmental variable types. Choosing Right Model Type model argument specifies underlying biological statistical assumptions causal pathway. MERLIN currently supports five distinct modes: “standard” (Default): comprehensive model assuming main genetic effects G×E interaction effects present exposure outcome pathways. “continuous_E”: specialized version standard model optimized continuous environmental variable. "discrete_E": specialized version standard model discrete binary environmental variables (e.g., sex) exposure outcome samples share environmental distribution. model requires additional parameter p_common, represents common proportion/probability environmental factor taking value 1 samples (.e., P(E=1)). "discrete_E_adj": adjusted version discrete environmental model situations proportion binary environmental variable differs exposure outcome samples (e.g., sex distributions differ two samples). model requires p_exp p_out, representing P(E=1) exposure outcome samples, respectively. model fitting, exposure GWAS GWIS estimates adjusted represent proportion E=1 outcome sample. “MO”: Designed practical scenarios outcome GWIS summary statistics unavailable. model drops requirement Gammah3, se4, rho_2. “”: Designed practical scenarios exposure GWIS summary statistics unavailable. model drops requirement gammah3, se2, rho_2. MCMC Control Parameters ensure reliability Bayesian estimation, MERLIN provides full control Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling process: maxIter: Total number Gibbs sampling iterations (default: 12000). burnin: Number initial iterations discarded allow chain reach stationary distribution (default: 5000). thin: thinning interval used reduce autocorrelation among posterior samples (default: 10). seed: Random seed fully reproducible MCMC results. MERLIN provides specialized "discrete" model, statistical evaluations demonstrated sample size ratio two environmental categories relatively balanced (.e., proportion close 1:1), default "standard" model highly robust yields almost identical causal estimates. title: Part 5: Model Fitting and Convergence Diagnostics
text: MERLIN relies Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods via Gibbs sampler, imperative verify Markov chains properly converged stationary distributions. Poor convergence indicates effect estimates may reliable. can visually inspect mixing convergence sampling chains main causal effect (\beta_1) interaction causal effect (\beta_4) using traceplot function.   Interpretation Guidelines Traceplots: Good Convergence: plot look like “hairy caterpillar,” chain rapidly mixing oscillating around stable mean value without obvious long-term trends drifting. Poor Convergence: chain exhibits slow wandering, gets stuck certain regions, shows distinct upward/downward trend, may need increase number MCMC iterations check input data extreme outliers. Note: using “MO” “” model, parameter estimation longer performed via MCMC procedure. Consequently, convergence diagnostics required.

h_g1 - h_g3 var_noise_y <- 1 - b1*b1 - h_b - b4*b4  # Construct the covariance matrix for the bivariate normal distribution cov_xy <- rhoxy * sqrt(var_noise_x * var_noise_y) sigma_noise <- matrix(c(var_noise_x, cov_xy,                         cov_xy, var_noise_y), ncol = 2)  # Generate correlated noise for X and Y noise_xy <- rmvnorm(n_exp + n_out, mean = c(0, 0), sigma = sigma_noise) noise_x <- noise_xy[, 1] noise_y <- noise_xy[, 2]  # Generate Exposure (X) X <- G %*% gamma_1x + GE %*% gamma_3x + 0.1 * E + noise_x  # Generate Outcome (Y)  Y <- X * b1 + G %*% beta_2 + X * E * b4 + 0.1 * E + noise_y  # Split into Exposure and Outcome datasets exp_gwas <- X[1:n_exp] exp_gwis <- X[1:n_exp] exp_E    <- E[1:n_exp]  out_gwas <- Y[(n_exp + 1):(n_exp + n_out)] out_gwis <- Y[(n_exp + 1):(n_exp + n_out)] out_E    <- E[(n_exp + 1):(n_exp + n_out)]

text: practice, researchers usually access summary statistics. define helper function get_sumstats run single-variant linear regressions extract effect sizes (\hat{\beta}) standard errors (SE).
code: get_sumstats <- function(G, pheno, interaction = FALSE, E = NULL) {   betas <- numeric(ncol(G))   ses <- numeric(ncol(G))      for(i in 1:ncol(G)) {     if(interaction) {       # GWIS: Model with GxE interaction term       model <- lm(pheno ~ G[, i] + E + G[, i]:E)       betas[i] <- coef(model)[4]       ses[i] <- summary(model)$coefficients[4, 2]     } else {       # GWAS: Standard additive genetic model       model <- lm(pheno ~ G[, i])       betas[i] <- coef(model)[2]       ses[i] <- summary(model)$coefficients[2, 2]     }   }   return(list(beta = betas, se = ses)) }  # Calculate Summary Statistics for Exposure Cohort exp_gwas_sum <- get_sumstats(G[1:n_exp, ], exp_gwas) exp_gwis_sum <- get_sumstats(G[1:n_exp, ], exp_gwis, interaction = TRUE, E = exp_E)  # Calculate Summary Statistics for Outcome Cohort out_gwas_sum <- get_sumstats(G[(n_exp + 1):(n_exp + n_out), ], out_gwas) out_gwis_sum <- get_sumstats(G[(n_exp + 1):(n_exp + n_out), ], out_gwis,                               interaction = TRUE, E = out_E)
